You're analyzing a match. Where do you start?

A) Recent form
B) Goal averages
C) Event frequency
D) Home/away split

Reply with your letter. The analysis starts with the right question.

#football #soccerstats
1/3 An 80% stat means an event happened in 8 out of 10 observations.
2/3 It doesn't mean an 80% chance next time. The sample can be small and the context can change.

3/3 Good analysis weighs frequency, context, sample size and uncertainty together. Data without interpretation can mislead.

#football #soccerstats

Virtual football generates data too.

But the analysis has to respect the competition format, the history available and how each environment behaves.

#football #soccerstats #esoccer

Matchday reminder:

The numbers don't predict football. They describe scenarios. Use them to understand the game, not to expect certainty.

#football #soccerstats

Since 2019, THE KING STATS has worked with football statistics.

The vision hasn't changed: read the numbers, understand the patterns, analyze opportunities with method.

thekingstats.com

Goals scored only tell part of a team's story.

Frequency, attacking volume and context explain how those goals happened, and whether they're likely to repeat.

#football #soccerstats

Before analyzing any match:

1. Home team's form at home
2. Away team's form away
3. Sample size of each
4. What changed recently

The overall average rarely tells the whole story.

#football #soccerstats

A team won 5 in a row. Are they in great form?

Depends on how they won, who they played and what the underlying numbers say.

What do you look at first?

#football #soccerstats

Frequency vs probability:

Frequency = what happened in a sample.
Probability = an estimate of what may happen.

Mixing them up breaks any analysis.

#football #soccerstats

In eSoccer, match length changes everything.

An 8-minute league and a 12-minute league produce completely different goal patterns. Never mix them in one average.

#football #soccerstats #esoccer

Big matchday. Before you watch, check:

• First-half tempo of both teams
• Goals for and against at this venue
• Sample size

Watch the game with the numbers in mind.

#football #soccerstats

Lesson of the week: track everything.

Without a record, you can't tell skill from luck. Every selection we make is logged and resolved publicly, green, red or void.

thekingstats.com

A team averaging 2.5 goals per game can still go three matches without scoring more than one.

Averages hide distribution. Always look at how often, not just how much.

#football #soccerstats

Pre-match checklist:

• Last 10, not last 3
• Home/away split
• Goals for AND against
• Schedule congestion

Context first, conclusions later.

#football #soccerstats

Which matters more for first-half goals?

A) Attacking team's early tempo
B) Defending team's early errors

Reply A or B and tell us why.

#football #soccerstats
1/3 Variance is why good analysis can have bad weeks.
2/3 Even a solid edge produces losing streaks over short samples. That's math, not failure.

3/3 Judge a method over hundreds of events, never over a weekend.

#football #soccerstats

eSoccer samples grow fast: dozens of matches per day.

That's an advantage for analysis, as long as you track player-level data, not just team names.

#football #soccerstats #esoccer

Live football and stats tell different stories in real time.

A 0-0 at halftime can hide a match with huge attacking volume. Look beyond the score.

#football #soccerstats

Our approach in one line:

Raw data free for everyone. Method applied automatically. Results tracked in the open.

Football, data and technology. thekingstats.com

Home and away are two different teams in the data.

Many sides change pace, shape and output completely on the road. Splitting the numbers matters.

#football #soccerstats

A strong attack vs a weak defense looks obvious on paper.

But check the opponents those numbers came from. Stats built against bottom teams don't transfer automatically.

#football #soccerstats

Unpopular opinion: a 1-0 win can be a worse performance than a 2-2 draw.

Result and performance are not the same thing. Agree or disagree?

#football #soccerstats

Mean vs median in football data:

One 6-0 thrashing can inflate a team's goal average for weeks. The median often tells a more honest story.

#football #soccerstats

eSoccer tip: the player matters more than the team badge.

Same club, different player, different numbers. Analyze who's on the controller.

#football #soccerstats #esoccer

Saturday rule: no stat is a guarantee.

Use data to filter, compare and understand. Football keeps its uncertainty, and that's why it's worth analyzing.

#football #soccerstats

Lesson of the week: a bad day doesn't break a method, and a great day doesn't prove one.

Only volume and time do. That's why we look at the month, not the match.

thekingstats.com

The first 15 minutes are statistically different from the rest of the first half.

Tempo, pressing and risk-taking change as teams settle. Period-specific data beats full-match averages.

#football #soccerstats

When two teams' numbers point in opposite directions, that's information too.

Not every match has a clear statistical edge. Knowing when to pass is part of the analysis.

#football #soccerstats

How many matches do you need before trusting a stat?

A) 5
B) 10
C) 20+
D) Depends on the stat

Reply below.

#football #soccerstats

Consistency beats peaks.

A team that hits a number in 7 of 10 games is often more readable than one that hits it 10 of 20 with huge swings.

#football #soccerstats
